title: Carrier Concentration vs. Temperature
description: Log-scale plot of the electron and hole concentrations in doped silicon from 50 K to 1000 K with the freeze-out, extrinsic, and intrinsic regimes shaded. The charge-neutrality equation is solved at every temperature for a chosen doping type and concentration, and a probe temperature gives numerical readouts.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics

chapter_title: Doping, Extrinsic Carriers, and the Fermi Level

educational.topic: Temperature regimes of carrier concentration in doped silicon
learningObjectives: Identify the freeze-out, extrinsic, and intrinsic regimes on a plot of n(T)
Predict the operating regime for a given doping level and temperature
Explain why heavier doping extends the extrinsic regime to higher temperature
prerequisites: Intrinsic carrier concentration and the law of mass action

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with a real-time log-scale plot and a probe-temperature readout
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict the regime at a given temperature and doping, then check it with the probe
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the regime at 77 K, 300 K, and 600 K for a given doping
Tabulate the boundary temperatures against doping
Verify n times p equals ni squared at the probe temperature

simulationModel.modelType: physics-based, numerical solution of charge neutrality
equations: n = Nc exp(-(Ec - Ef)/kT), p = Nv exp(-(Ef - Ev)/kT)
Nd+/Nd = 1/(1 + 2 exp((Ef - Ed)/kT)), Na-/Na = 1/(1 + 4 exp((Ea - Ef)/kT))
ni(T) = sqrt(Nc Nv) exp(-Eg(T)/2kT), Eg(T) Varshni
assumptions: Silicon with a single dopant species (phosphorus or boron, 45 meV)
Nc = 2.86e19 and Nv = 3.10e19 cm^-3 at 300 K, scaled as T^1.5
Eg(0) set to 1.175 eV so that ni(300 K) = 9.65e9 cm^-3
Freeze-out boundary at 90 percent ionization; intrinsic boundary where ni(T) equals the doping
limitations: Isolated dopant levels and Boltzmann statistics: not valid for degenerate doping, so the slider stops at 1e18 cm^-3
